transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Evan Marshall (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Zhou (Redwood SE), Tom Reyes (Head of ML, Magnolia), Sara Nguyen (Infra Lead, Magnolia), Isabel Moore (PM, Magnolia)
---
[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Evan, I'm the AE on this account, Priya and Liam are our SEs who will run the technical POC.
[00:12] Tom: Hi all — Tom here. high level we want to validate an inference path for our supply-optimization feature. main concerns are latency for interactive queries and cost for high-throughput batch scoring.
[00:25] Sara: And from infra we need to be clear on network setup, whether we can use Redwood Hosted or need dedicated based on audited data flows. we also have a KMS requirement.
[00:35] Priya: Great — we'll cover success criteria, workloads, benchmarks, and then deployment options. quick note: transcript may have little artefacts; sorry for any mis-heard acronyms.
[00:45] Evan: First question — what are your acceptance criteria? Tom?
[00:48] Tom: For us success is three folds: 1) median latency under 250ms for interactive prompts with 512 token seq, 2) batch throughput of 1k requests per minute for nightly scoring with acceptable cost target — roughly $0.0008 per inference historically, and 3) auditability: we need immutable logs and key management for encryption. plus a rollout plan to gradua— gradual canary.
[01:20] Isabel: timeline wise we need a working pilot in 6 weeks and decision to go to prod in 12 weeks if POC looks good.
[01:30] Liam: Ok thanks. rough follow up — do you have current traffic shape or example logs we can use to size?
[01:37] Tom: We can export. main pattern is spikes at 9am/3pm in our timezone, median qps about 10 sustained but tails to 120 qps during peak for the interactive front end; batch windows hit 2k qps but short lived. We'll share two weeks.
[01:52] Priya: Perfect. that's helpful — for sizing we'll run two benchmark profiles: interactive and batch. interactive will simulate concurrency and token length distribution; batch will validate sustained throughput and KV cache warm up. note: our runtime benefits from prefix caching for repeated contexts.
[02:12] Sara: Quick question — if we choose Hosted for speed, what about VPC and KMS requirements?
[02:18] Evan: Hosted supports customer-owned KMS via a managed integration in some regions; however full VPC peering and private network path is typically supported on Dedicated or Private. we'll enumerate exact constraints in the security doc.
[02:31] Tom: Are there hard guarantees on data retention and audit logs for Hosted? our compliance team expects retention for 12 months and auditable access logs.
[02:40] Priya: We can enable longer retention as an add-on and exportable audit logs; Hosted provides those but in some accounts we recommend Dedicated to keep logs isolated at the tenant level. small caveat: "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes labelled Dedi in our notes — apologies if the transcript munges that.
[02:55] Evan: Let's move to benchmarks — what metrics matter? Latency p50/p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, cold-start behavior for KV caches, and degradation under a noisy neighbor scenario. anything else?
[03:10] Tom: Accuracy/regression vs baseline model matter too — we need a small eval set so P0 is that the model's outputs don't regress more than 2% on our scoreboard.
[03:20] Isabel: And can we measure fallbacks? e.g., if primary model is slow, how gracefully Redwood routes to a smaller variant — is that automatic?
[03:29] Priya: We have policy routing and automatic fallback; during the POC we can enable a canary variant path and measure quality delta. we'll include that in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:40] [04:00] Speaker 1 (unlabeled): slight echo — sorry.
[04:10] Evan: On cost modeling — we'll produce cost per inference under multiple packing/batching profiles and show the tradeoffs of quantization on latency and quality. Priya will run a quick quantization sensitivity test.
[04:22] Priya: For the technical plan I propose: Day 0-2 prep (logs + runbook), Day 3-4 quick hosted baseline runs, Day 5-8 dedicated profile runs (simulate reserved pool), Day 9-10 final eval and handoff — that's the 10-day micro benchmark plan. stretched across their calendar it'll fit the 6-week pilot.
[04:45] Tom: Sounds good. question on dedicated: does Redwood Dedicated require a minimum reserved commit? and how long to provision?
[04:52] Evan: Dedicated has a minimum monthly commitment; provisioning time is typically 7-14 days depending on GPU availability and region. for pilots we can often offer a short-term dedicated pool for evaluation without a long-term sign-up, but it depends on capacity. we'll note that in the offer.
[05:10] Sara: On networking — if we go Dedicated in our VPC, how is peering handled? we use AWS but want cross-account restrictions.
[05:18] Liam: For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private subnets; networking design doc will include IP allowlists, NATing patterns, and flow logs. for Private on-prem, we do an air-gapped appliance and a customer control plane.
[05:32] Tom: Could you outline where customers usually land? like percentage who start hosted and then move?
[05:37] Evan: Anecdotally many customers start Hosted for speed-to-value; about 30% transition to Dedicated as they need stronger isolation or cost predictability; a smaller subset (~10%) adopt Private for regulated workloads. varies by industry.
[05:52] Isabel: Cost concern — how much does quantization reduce GPU footprint in practice?
[05:58] Priya: 8-bit quantization commonly reduces memory and can increase packing allowing more concurrency per GPU. end-to-end cost drop depends on model and workload but we've seen 30-60% unit cost reduction with careful tuning and eval for quality impact. we'll include sample numbers in the spreadsheet.
[06:15] Tom: For SLAs — what Uptime and latency SLOs do Dedicated and Hosted have?
[06:21] Evan: Hosted has tiered SLAs for paid plans; Dedicated has stronger, contract-backed SLOs including targeted p99 latency windows. we'll send the SLA summary.
[06:30] Sara: Security checklist: SSO, SAML, RBAC, SAML just to confirm?
[06:36] Priya: Yes SSO via SAML or OIDC supported, RBAC roles in Console, audit logs, and optional SIEM integrations. we'll attach our security pack (SOC2, ISO docs) in the follow-up.
[06:50] [07:00] Tom: One more thing — network egress costs when using Hosted, do you surface that?
[07:04] Evan: Egress depends on region; we surface predicted egress and include it in costing. if egress is a blocker customers often choose Dedicated in same cloud region or Private to avoid cross-cloud charges.
[07:18] Isabel: Back to success criteria — can we write a short acceptance rubric so both sides sign off?
[07:23] Evan: Yes; propose a 6-point rubric: latency p50/p95 thresholds, throughput target in batch, cost per inference band, no regressions >2% on eval, audit/logging available and accessible, and deployment/rollout plan validated with a canary. I'll draft that and attach.
[07:40] Tom: Good. in the POC we want a gating rule: if p95 > 600ms on interactive we'll consider Dedicated or model changes.
[07:49] Priya: noted, we'll instrument p95 and tail latencies.
[07:55] [08:00] Liam: A minor note on benchmarks — we should run synthetic load and a replay of real logs to exercise caching patterns. for KV cache we'll measure cost reduction after warmup.
[08:12] Tom: Replay will be our preference. we'll sanitize logs and give to you.
[08:18] Isabel: timeline — after you get logs how quickly can you produce first draft results?
[08:22] Priya: If we get logs by Mon 10/26, we can run hosted quick tests by the 28th and a dedicated simulation by 10/30; we'll publish initial results in 48 hours after the runs.
[08:36] Evan: Risks: 1) data residency/legal might block Hosted in certain geos, 2) underprovisioned Dedicated could cause higher cost if traffic peaks are underestimated, 3) model quality regressions with quantization. we will call these out in the runbook.
[08:55] Sara: Regarding KMS: our compliance wants HSM-backed keys. does Redwood support HSM?
[09:02] Priya: We integrate with customer-managed KMS; HSM-backed keys via AWS CloudHSM or external HSMs are supported in Dedicated and Private setups. Hosted has limited HSM support regionally; we'll mark that constraint.
[09:18] Tom: For Private — what does on-prem requirement look like? disk, GPU types, networking?
[09:24] Liam: On-prem Private is a packaged runtime, we need GPU inventory (A10x, H100, or equivalent), minimum network egress, and a control-plane connection for updates if allowed. we'll provide an install checklist.
[09:38] Evan: Okay — pivot to the quick experiment plan details. Priya?
[09:42] Priya: Step one: ingest logs and produce a traffic profile. step two: create small eval prompt set for quality checks. step three: run three profiles: hosted baseline on our verified model, dedicated profile simulating reserved GPU pool and autoscale, and a degraded/noisy neighbor case. metrics captured: p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost, regression delta, cache warmup curve. we'll record videos of runs and share dashboards.
[10:10] Tom: Nice. question — how do we simulate cold start vs warm caches?
[10:14] Priya: We'll do a controlled run that zeroes KV caches between test windows and measure the first 1000 requests separately.
[10:22] Isabel: can Redwood instrument token-level cost tracing? we want to map which routes cost more.
[10:27] Evan: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdowns. we'll include a screenshot in the artifacts.
[10:36] [11:00] Speaker 2: slight background noise.
[11:08] Sara: On procurement — if the POC looks good, what is typical contracting timeline for Dedicated?
[11:12] Evan: Once committed, procurement often takes 2-6 weeks for legal and PO. Dedicated start depends on provisioning but budget sign-off is the slowest part.
[11:22] Tom: Any reference customers in manufacturing or industrials? we prefer someone similar.
[11:27] Evan: We can share two references in industrials; I'll include contact names — I think one is willing to discuss deployment mode migration.
[11:36] Priya: small technical note: for throughput optimization we can suggest micro-batching and continuous batching; for interactive we favor lower-latency kernels and fewer packing.
[11:47] Tom: good. also we want to ensure support model during pilot — who is our SE contact during runs?
[11:52] Evan: Priya will be primary; Liam as backup; we'll also have on-call infra for the high-load run.
[12:00] Isabel: Can Redwood do a short cost projection comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for our expected 12-week burn?
[12:06] Evan: Yes, we'll run a 12-week synthetic burn with your traffic profile and show cost curves and break-even points, factoring in Dedicated reservation discounts.
[12:17] Tom: For the POC acceptance— besides the rubric, who signs? our PM and Infra lead?
[12:22] Isabel: I'll coordinate sign-off from Product and Tom will validate ML qual.
[12:27] Evan: Great. last thing — any hard no-go items?
[12:30] Sara: Can't open-source patient/financial PII to third party; data must be anonymized for the POC.
[12:35] Priya: Understood — we'll only run on sanitized logs and can set up a private pipeline if needed.
[12:42] Evan: Ok wrapping up. recap of immediate deliverables: Evan shares benchmark sheet + runbook; Magnolia to share logs; schedule perf run. we'll aim to hit the 6-week pilot kickoff.
[12:57] Tom: thanks everyone. excited to see the numbers.
[13:00] Evan: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
---
References shared in call (links noted in follow-up): Benchmark spreadsheet (template), Redwood security pack (SOC2 + ISO), Quick-run harness repo, Example SLA summary.
